# GazeControl — Progress Board

Working memory for GazeControl (data-driven gaze control for virtual agents in a
triad conversation: two virtual agents + the user; gaze patterns collected before
turn-taking in real triad conversations drive the agents' gaze).

**Source of truth: this file.** `progress.html` is auto-generated from it on every
commit by the `progress-board` skill's pre-commit hook — never hand-edit the HTML.

Status legend: `[ ]` todo · `[~]` in progress · `[x]` done · `[!]` blocked.
Completed tasks carry a `_(done YYYY-MM-DD · <short-commit>)_` tag (the commit that
finished them, for history tracking); the dashboard keeps full detail for the most
recent few completed items and compacts older ones.

    - **The bag carries no UV mapping.** All 161 of its vertices (129 new ones plus the inner-lip rim that was merged into them) collapse onto UV (0, 0), so the whole cavity samples a single texel — the bottom-left corner of whichever albedo the agent wears. That corner is RGB(77, 85, 84) in the stock 4096² SMPL-X atlas (reads black) but RGB(245, 246, 241) in the 512² SMPLitex one, which is exactly why Agent A looked right and Agent B looked grey. Nothing else uses that texel: the nearest mapped UV is 0.029 away (15 px at 512², 120 px at 4096²).
    - `SmplxMouthInteriorSubmesh` (an `AssetPostprocessor`) moves every triangle whose three vertices all sit on UV (0, 0) — exactly 288 of the mesh's 21196 — onto submesh 1 and assigns `SMPLX-MouthInterior.mat` (URP Lit, base colour 0.055/0.02/0.02). There are no partially-mapped seam triangles, so the rule has no edge cases. Idempotent across reimports, and the scene needed no overrides: the second material slot is inherited from the model prefab.
    - **The FBX swap was a true drop-in.** Same node names (plus 15 unbound `*_end` leaf bones from Blender), same single source material, and the 520 blendshapes identical in name and order — so visemes stay at 506-519. ## Decisions

- 2026-08-02 — **The mouth interior is real geometry separated by UV, not a blocker object.** The re-exported SMPL-X FBX carries a mouth bag, but it is unmapped — every one of its vertices sits on UV (0, 0) — so it rendered in whatever colour the agent's albedo happens to hold in its bottom-left texel: dark in the stock atlas, near-white in the SMPLitex one. Splitting those 288 triangles onto their own submesh at import time (`SmplxMouthInteriorSubmesh`) makes the cavity texture-independent, so any future SMPLitex agent gets a correct mouth for free. Chosen over splitting the material in Blender (a round trip per model revision) and over painting the texture corner dark (needs repeating for every new agent texture). The `MouthCavity`/`MouthBackdrop` blockers and their tuning menu are deleted.

- 2026-07-30 — **Baseline A is pure Shintani: no hand-authored turn-boundary overrides, no mutual-gaze breaking** (user's call). `baseline-spec.md` §2 prescribes both, but they belong to the superseded Mutlu/Goffman baseline. The `changing`/`holding` conditioning is the empirically-estimated version of the same effect, and a scripted turn-yielding gaze inside Baseline A would fire in exactly the window the proposed method overrides — contaminating the comparison and, since A is also the proposed method's substrate, both conditions at once. Mutual-gaze breaking is left out as one un-corpus-derived parameter that the measured 0.77-0.88 jump-to-aversion makes unnecessary; it stays checkable because `mutual_gaze_*` is logged.

- 2026-07-30 — **Baseline A's fitted parameters ship as a committed JSON config**, `Assets/GazeControl/Resources/BaselineAParameters.json`, generated by `Tools/build_baseline_a_params.py` from the git-ignored `Research/corpora`. Config over constants is what `baseline-spec.md` §2 asks for, and it means a fresh clone can run the condition without the corpus. The generator is committed so the numbers stay re-derivable.

- 2026-07-30 — **Aversion re-target intervals come from an empirical quantile table, not a fitted law.** Direction segments are clipped by the ends of their aversion, so 17% fall below the corpus's 0.1 s fixation floor while the tail reaches 16.6 s; a lognormal truncated at the floor would inflate the mean interval by about a quarter. The table spans p0-p99 (top 1% = 2.4-16.6 s truncated, and the governing aversion dwell truncates it in practice anyway). Only un-clipped segments are fitted, since the generator clips its own last segment the same way the corpus did.
  - The corpus README's 0.939 s re-targeting estimate (OLS of direction count on aversion duration) is **not** used: sampling intervals from the observed segment distribution reproduces the observed 2.12 directions per aversion by construction, whereas 0.939 s would give 1.8.

- 2026-07-13 — Gaze control and agent motion are both **data-driven**, from gaze behaviour patterns collected before turn-taking in real triad conversations.

- 2026-07-30 — **Q3 answered: sampled aversion in every condition**, including the proposed method. `GazeRole.None` stops recentering the eyes and becomes a sampled direction, so the animation layer is identical across conditions (§0.1, §5.3). This visibly changes the signed-off 7e demo — accepted. No guesswork needed: `aversion_direction/` gives 9-way marginals per role, the 9×9 first→second conditional, and **measured az/el per bin** (lateral ≈ ±20° yaw; up bins ≈ +11° pitch, down bins ≈ −13°), which land inside `baseline-spec.md` §1's guessed 15-30° / 10-20° band.
  - Re-targeting cadence: the corpus README claims 0.6-0.94 s "bracketing Shintani's 0.7 s", but `aversion_segments.csv` gives per-segment **median 0.22 s, mean 0.36 s** (2-3 segments per event, ~0.75 s mean aversion). Sample segment durations from the empirical distribution rather than any constant, which sidesteps the conflict.

- 2026-07-30 — **Q4 answered: minimal gaze-direction layer, no blink.** Body motion is pre-defined mocap from file, so the layer's only job is gaze direction. See the task entry for what is kept vs dropped.

- 2026-07-30 — **Corpus event table delivered and validated**, at `Research/corpora/` (git-ignored; regenerate from `F:\Code\scnpro\prototype\prototype`). It answers all three outstanding data questions and changes two plan assumptions:
  - **Use lognormal durations, not χ².** The corpus authors tested both: across role × target × `min_dwell`, **0 of 45 cells** give χ² an interior mode (fitted `dn` 0.88–1.78), and lognormal fits better in 8 of 9 cells (mean KS 0.051 vs 0.070). Shintani's χ² degenerates toward exponential on this data. This lands back on `baseline-spec.md` §2's original log-normal choice. Also: `dloc` is an artifact of the `min_dwell` filter (0.1 s), not a property of gaze.
  - **The "twitchy dwell" worry is resolved.** Real durations are roughly double the geometric ones implied by the transition matrix — mean 0.65–1.11 s, median 0.40–0.58 s, p90 1.3–2.5 s (vs 0.30–0.53 s geometric), with a genuine long tail. Gaze at the *speaker* is longest (~1.1 s), matching Shintani and Mutlu's ~0.98 s.
  - **`ad` is NOT an annotated addressee** — it is `second_speaker`, a hindsight label for whoever actually spoke next, which participants did not have at the time. `first_speaker[k] == second_speaker[k-1]` holds only **47.9%** of the time, so these do not form a floor-passing chain. `sp` is sound; `ad` is loose and `sd` inherits that looseness. Shintani's Addressee is a different variable — say so when reporting.
  - **Aversion direction was recovered** from the raw head-mounted eye tracker (34/38 sessions) rather than annotated: 9-way marginals per role plus the 9×9 first→second conditional. Measured re-targeting period 0.6–0.94 s **brackets Shintani's 0.7 s constant**. Note our distribution is flatter than theirs and lateral-down dominates (ld/rd ≈ 0.15) rather than pure down; `u` is rarest (0.05).
  - Other caveats from the corpus README worth carrying: `changing` covers 57.8% of gazed frames (dense turn annotation — narrow via `frames_to_turn` if needed); 24.26% of fixations outlive their governing event (`spans_events`); censoring is negligible (0.15%, drop it).

- 2026-07-27 — **Baseline A supplies the proposed method's substrate** (user's choice): outside the 1 s pre-turn window the proposed agent *is* a Baseline A agent, and the paper's pattern only overrides inside the window. Cleanest isolation of the contribution — the conditions then differ only where the claim is. Consequence: the transition matrix and dwell distributions are on the critical path for two of three conditions, not one.

- 2026-07-27 — **Baseline A's parameters come from our own corpus**, not the literature table in `baseline.md` §2 — which is what that spec itself calls "strictly better". Source: `F:\Code\scnpro\prototype\prototype\output\transition_full_conv_legacymap\` (38 sessions, 2.0 M frames @ 60 fps). Two structural findings the literature guess misses: (a) **star topology** — leaving a person, ~90% of jumps go to aversion, not to the other person, so direct person→person shifts are rare; (b) our triad **averts far more** than the published proportions (speaker 0.445 vs 0.40, listener 0.397 vs 0.25, side participant 0.411 vs 0.25) and looks at the speaker much less (0.422 vs 0.65). EoT type (interruption/overlap/turn-taking) is irrelevant — max deviation from pooled is 0.0076, so use pooled.

- 2026-07-27 — The stored matrix is **per-frame at 60 Hz** (diagonals ~0.95), so Baseline A uses the derived **jump chain** (off-diagonals renormalised) plus separate dwell distributions. Reconstructing occupancy as `π·E[dwell]` normalised reproduces the observed occupancy to within 0.004 across all three roles, which validates the semi-Markov formulation — and removes the "solve for a matrix matching the §2 proportions" step from the plan entirely.

- 2026-07-27 — **Baseline B runs on the existing animation layer**; the §4 rewrite is a separate, later task. B uses person-targets only, so the rewrite buys it nothing, and changing `GazeController` would alter the appearance of the signed-off 7e demo unverified.

- 2026-07-27 — **Voice activity is measured from the clip waveform at the playback position**, not `AudioSource.GetOutputData` (which is distance-attenuated, so detection would depend on where the listener stands). When the audio engine's `timeSamples` is not advancing, an internal playback clock takes over — without that fallback a dead output device yields a complete, plausible-looking gaze log in which nobody ever speaks.

- 2026-07-27 — **Condition wiring lives in a menu command** (`GazeControl → Set Up Gaze Conditions`), not in the committed scene, while the scene carries in-flight MouthCavity edits. Note: Unity auto-saved the scene on entering Play Mode during testing, so the wiring had to be reverted by hand afterwards — expect this if you test the same way.

- 2026-07-26 — Agents get distinct appearances via **per-agent materials + SMPLitex SMPL-X textures**. SMPLitex outputs (512², no eyeball UV island) are used as-is for body/face; the eye disc is copied from the default 4096² SMPL-X albedo since both eyes share that single UV island. Agent A stays on the default `SMPLX-Male-URP`.
